result.headline_THE_MACHINE_CONSTANT: Eager submission cost is LINEAR in dispatch count with R2 = 0.99999 at 0.16783 ms per node. Batched, the marginal cost of an added node falls to 0.01084 ms. So on this machine and runtime a WITHIN-COMMAND-BUFFER DISPATCH costs about 11 microseconds while a CROSS-COMMAND-BUFFER SUBMISSION costs about 157 microseconds -- a ratio of 14.5x. That is an actionable threshold: any kernel doing less than ~0.16 ms of GPU work is dominated by its own submission if it is submitted alone.
result.this_quantifies_the_earlier_refutation: ACCELERATOR_SYNC_CORRECTION.json refuted 'launch count' and named host round trips instead, but only as a ratio. The constant explains the magnitudes: collapsing 3 dispatches to 1 saves 2 x 11 us = 22 us, which is nothing against a 500 us operation, while collapsing 3 submissions to 1 saves 2 x 157 us = 314 us, which is the 2.3x that was observed. The two experiments used different work and agree.
result.cross_check_one_agrees_one_does_not: The reduction at 2^20 went 0.555 ms eager to 0.241 ms batched over 2 removed submissions = 0.157 ms each, which matches this constant exactly from entirely different work. At 2^24 the same arithmetic gives 0.073 ms, which does NOT match. The constant is therefore NOT universal -- at 2^24 there is enough real GPU work to overlap part of the host round trip. Recorded because a constant that fails one of its two cross-checks is a constant with a stated domain, not a law.
result.concurrency_is_the_SMALLER_half: Independent branches DO overlap, and it is worth much less than batching. Fan beats chain by 1.09x at k=8 and 1.16x at k=16 at 2^20 with clean arms, and on the MARGINAL node the saving is 1.356x at 2^20 and 1.495x at 4096. So of the two things CUDA graphs and streams offer, this runtime gives most of the ORDERING/BATCHING value and only a little of the CONCURRENCY value. A graph here is worth building for submission batching, not for parallelism, and the two are kept as separate fields.
result.what_the_gate_refused: Every fan-vs-chain comparison at n=4096 returned NO_CLAIM: the arms carry 10-25% IQR because the whole measurement is a fraction of a millisecond. The 4096 fan/chain ratio LOOKS the same as the 2^20 one (1.16x at k=16) but is not claimed, because a ratio that agrees with a claimed result is still not a measurement. Only the linear fit is quoted at that size, and it is quoted because R2 = 0.99999 across 5 points is evidence the per-point noise is not.

claim_boundary: One elementwise kernel shape, f32, two sizes, k up to 16, MLX 0.32.1 on one machine. AirGraph records a DAG and executes it in ONE submission -- it does NOT implement CUDA stream or event SEMANTICS (no independent ordered queues, no cross-stream events, no host callbacks, no graph update or instantiation reuse), so RUNTIME.streams_and_events stays PARTIAL and nothing here may be called CUDA graph support. The concurrency measured is whatever the runtime does with independent work in one buffer, not a scheduler we control.
